Can you share a recommended config (max retries, temperature/top_p settings, and whether you use sampling vs. greedy decoding for schema enforcement)?

3) Observability: can you export the per-request schema pass rate and the exact model variant used in each fallback? We need these for our audit logs.

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks for the great questions. Below is our recommended approach and concrete config guidance you can use during the eval. Happy to walk through this on the sync.

1) Schema validation & repair flow (recommended):
- Primary: use function-calling / structured output mode where the model returns a typed JSON object matching a supplied schema (we pass a JSON Schema + function signature).
- Server-side: always run strict JSON Schema validation (we validate Draft-07 / 2019-09). If validation fails, attempt up to 1 automatic "repair" pass using our deterministic parser (minimal heuristics: trailing commas, unclosed braces, common quote mismatches).
- If repair fails, do a single retry with deterministic decoding (temperature=0, top_p=1.0, max_new_tokens limited to expected payload length + 50).
- If retry still fails, escalate to fallback policy: either run model with a different family (e.g., redwood-v2-medium -> redwood-v2-xl) or send to human review based on confidence thresholds.

2) Retry policy & idempotency:
- Recommended retries: 1 automatic repair attempt + 1 deterministic generation retry (total 2 attempts). This keeps token cost bounded while improving schema pass rate.
- Decoding config for schema enforcement: temperature=0, top_p=1.0, repetition_penalty=1.1, max_new_tokens configured per schema (we set a hard cap).
- For action-invoking tool calls (create_order), we recommend generating a signed operation token in the model output (a deterministic idempotency key) and validating that on your side before executing external actions. Redwood can also produce an action_preview payload for manual confirmation when required.

3) Observability & audit logs:
- We persist per-request metadata: model_variant, prompt_hash, schema_pass (bool), parse_errors (string), latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, and run_id. These are exportable via the Console and via our API with the audit retention package.

4) Model recommendations for your workload (based on the call + our initial sample):
- redwood-v2-medium: good latency/cost balance; target for 90-95% schema pass in zero-shot structured extraction.
- redwood-v2-xl: higher accuracy for edge cases and complex nested schemas; use as fallback or for canonicalization runs.
- For high-volume low-latency decisioning (if <200ms required), we can provide quantized variants (redwood-v2-medium-q4) and batching profiles; tradeoffs documented in attached benchmark PDF.

5) Eval instructions and prompt-set:
- Use the attached avery_prompt_set_v1.json as the canonical test set. Run 200 samples through the harness with the following config:

CONFIG SNIPPET (text):
- model: redwood-v2-medium
- temperature: 0
- top_p: 1.0
- max_new_tokens: dependent on schema (recommend +50 tokens margin)
- retries: repair=1, generation_retry=1
- schema_validation: Draft-07 strict
- log_level: debug (capture parse_errors)

6) Benchmarks & links:
- Benchmarks PDF (attached) includes per-model median latency, p95/p99, and schema pass rates for our structured extraction workloads.
- Eval harness and scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/tree/avery-case
- Shared Drive with raw results & dashboards: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AveryBenchmarksLink

If you want, during the tech sync we can run a gated live pass on 20 records and show schema pass/fail and the repair flow in real-time.

Attachments referenced: avery_prompt_set_v1.json, model_benchmarks_2027Q2.pdf

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
